warnings: Both floor levels are drawn on one sheet (left = ชั้นล่าง, right = ชั้นบน). Extracted as one elements[] array with a level field on each element, per the same convention house 24 used for its equivalent S-02 sheet.

Floor-1 (left, 10.70m tall) matches house 24's ground-floor plan exactly in beam layout: B2/B6/B7/B3A/B3/B3B/B1/B4/Bx running จ-ข (10.70m, with the B4 strip from ค to ข at 4.00m and a 1.50m extension to ก), and a small 0.20m Bx stub below row ข. No dummy grid was needed for floor 1 — every beam endpoint lands on a printed grid line.

Floor 2 (right, 10.70m tall) is a DIFFERENT layout from floor 1: the B4 strip is replaced by a B5 beam at grid 2 running from row ค down to row ก, and the B1/Bx/B1 box south of row ข is replaced by an S1 slab panel plus a 1.30m B1 strip south of row ข. Both floors' beams were extracted independently and are not merged.

Row ก exists only on the ground floor (the house steps down to a carport/porch at that level) — floor 2's B2 beam runs จ-ง-ค-ง-จ (10.70m) with no extension to row ก, confirmed by the floor-2 plan's own dimension chain ending at row ค.

S0/S1/S1 slab markers on floor 1 (S0 x2 above row จ, S1 near grid 3) and S1 x2 on floor 2 (near grid 3 and south of row ข) are point-style slab-panel markers (circled tags sitting inside bays, not line-drawn slab edges) — recorded as element_type 'slab' with approximate grid_refs and no span, per §4's point-vs-line distinction. Their exact extents are not dimensioned on this sheet.

warnings: The footing plan shows a 3x5 grid of footings (rows จ-ก, columns 1-3) with 2 distinct column marks (C1, C2) and 7 distinct footing marks (F2-F8) — the exact same layout and mark count as house #3's S-01, but with different individual mark assignments (e.g. house #3's row จ has F4/F5/F4, this house's has F4/F5/F4 too — coincidence, not a copy). Every footing position was read directly from the printed mark labels at each grid intersection.

Pattern 'plan' was used for all four structural subtasks (footing/beam/column/slab) as of 2026-08-28, closing the schema section-1 plan-family split (beam_plan/footing_plan/roof_frame_plan) that section introduced — the split never got used in existing data because every legacy file had been bulk-renamed to 'plan' and nothing new was written into the new values. Decided from what the sheet DRAWS (footing marks = footing_plan, beam marks = beam_plan, roof-framing marks = roof_frame_plan), not from the filename alone, and never as a residual fallback — that was the reason the split was created in the first place. Reason: legacy files predate the split and every sheet_code in this house is structural, so no sheet_code ambiguity remains.

This house's foundation system is pile footing (เสาเข็ม) — see the structural notes section 5 ('เสาเข็ม ให้ใช้เสาเข็มคอนกรีตอัดแรง...') — so these are pile-cap footings, not spread footings. Recorded as element_type 'footing' per the existing house-06 precedent (same naming convention used there for a pile-footing S-01), not a new 'pile_cap' type — flagging this since the element_type glossary does carry a separate 'pile_cap' value and this is a judgment call, not a direct spec match.

warnings: This is a COMBINED sheet — two views on one page, floor 1 (left) and floor 2 (right). Both are extracted into one elements[] array, distinguished by floor_level. The two floors have DIFFERENT beam layouts (floor 2 adds B5 and drops the B4/B1 extension to grid ก), so they could not be merged into one entry per mark.

The stairwell (grid ง-ค, columns 1-2) is the SAME on both floors — one B1 vertical on col 1, one B7A vertical on col 2, both spanning ง to ค, with B3 horizontal at ง and ค. Recorded once per floor as separate entries since they are physically different members on different floors, not duplicates.

Floor 1 has an extension south of grid ข (columns 1-2) to grid ก: B4 verticals on col 1 and col 2 from ข to ก, a B1 horizontal at grid ก, and two Bx slabs on either side of the col-2 line. Floor 2 does NOT have this extension — its south edge is grid ข. This is the main difference between the two floors' plans.

Floor 2's extension east of grid 2 (columns 2-3, row ข-ก) has a different layout from floor 1: B5 vertical on grid 2, B1 horizontal at grid ข, B4 verticals on col 3, and an S1 slab. Floor 1 instead has B4 verticals on col 1 and col 2 from ข to ก there. Both are recorded as printed.

Bx appears on both floors with a Thai parenthetical '(ข.พ.)' next to it on the floor-2 view — read as 'พื้นระเบียง' (balcony slab) per the architectural sheet's own legend (หน้า06), consistent with the balcony/terrace locations (west of col 1 at row ง-ค, and south of grid ข in the col 2-3 bay on floor 2). Recorded as element_type 'slab' with the printed text kept in note.

S0 (two circles, north of row จ, columns 1-2) appears only on floor 1 — likely a roof/terrace slab over the ground-floor room below, consistent with S0 being the 'พื้นหลังคา' (roof slab) type per หน้า06.0 Not present on floor 2 (which IS the roof level structurally, but carries no S0 marker there).

The 0.90/0.95/1.30/0.50/0.20/1.30 offset dimensions printed on both views are sub-grid dimensions resolving the stairwell and balcony projections (e.g. 0.90 west of grid 1, 0.50 east of grid 3) — not used to define dummy grid lines since they are projection offsets, not structural grid lines, and the beams at those edges (B6, B3A/B3B) still resolve to the main grid + dummy grid 1'/3' already defined in the master.
